deep.reconstruction:
The page is a laboratory sheet of magnetometer scale readings, probably from the Göttingen magnetic or induction experiments of the 1830s with Weber. Each number is a reading of the scale seen in the mirror of a suspended magnet; the previous page fixes the scale–mirror distance at 4884.1 mm. The only mathematics is arithmetic means and half-differences, used to separate the effect of a large bar ('großer Stab') placed near the instrument with its north pole down (N unten, NU) or up (N oben, NO).

(1) 18 March: two readings, mean (125.671 + 125.541)/2 = 125.606.

(2) 20 March, large bar with N down: five readings 121.602, 122.047, 122.724, 121.657, 122.445. Mean = 610.475/5 = 122.095.

(3) 21 March, large bar with N up: five readings 128.984, 129.776, 130.150, 129.715, 130.422. Mean written as 129.807.
- Gauss joins the two series with a brace and takes 'Mittel' (122.095 + 129.807)/2 = 125.951. This is the reading with the reversible, polarity-dependent effect of the bar removed.
- [my step] The half-difference (129.807 − 122.095)/2 = 3.856 divisions is the polarity-dependent deflection.

(4) Same day, large bar removed ('Gr Stab entfernt'): readings 127.524, 127.723, 126.566, 127.558, 125.721. Mean = 635.092/5 = 127.018.
- [my step] The bar-free reading differs from the NU/NO mean by 127.018 − 125.951 = 1.067. That is either a polarity-independent effect of the bar (e.g. induced magnetism) or drift in the declination between the series.

(5) 22 March, without the large bar ('ohne gr Stab'): readings 128.99(2), 128.796, 129.258, 128.688, 128.989. Mean = 128.9446.
- Single readings with the bar: 126.457 (NU) and 130.585 (NO).
- [my steps] Their mean is 128.521, so bar-free minus mean = 0.4236. Their half-difference is 2.064.

The next page (24 March: 130.554 N.O, 126.447 N.U, about 128.5 with the bar removed) continues the same scheme. It also tabulates the change of elongation produced by repeated 'Stöße' (impulses), so the sheet belongs to the ballistic/induction measurements.
errors: 21 March mean: the five values as read sum to 649.047, so the mean is 129.8094, not 129.807. The written mean would follow if the fourth value were 129.705 instead of 129.715. Either the digit is misread or Gauss made a slip of 0.002 in the mean. The consequent 'Mittel' 125.951 is correct given 129.807; with 129.809 it would be 125.952.

No other arithmetic errors. 18 March (125.606), 20 March (122.095) and 'Stab entfernt' (127.018) all check. The 22 March mean 128.9446 checks only if the first value is 128.992 (see transcription corrections).

results.what: Arithmetic means of repeated magnetometer scale readings, and reversal of the bar's polarity (N down / N up). Averaging the two orientations eliminates the polarity-dependent deflection; comparing with the bar removed isolates any polarity-independent effect.
results.modern_name: Averaging of repeated observations; reversal (commutation) method for eliminating systematic effects
results.usually_credited_to: Standard experimental practice; magnetometric reversal methods were systematized by Gauss and Weber in the 1830s

deep.surprise_reason: Raw observational data with simple means. The reversal technique is well documented in Gauss–Weber magnetic work; there is nothing mathematically new.

checkable.asserts: equals 129.8094, not Gauss's 129.807 (slip or misread digit)
equals 128.9446, confirming the first 22 March value is 128.992
equals 128.9346, so the machine reading 128.942 is inconsistent with Gauss's mean
equals 2.064, the half-difference NO−NU on 22 March

transcription_corrections: 22 March, first value: read 128.992 (written over another digit), not 128.942. Only 128.992 reproduces the written mean 128.9446.
21 March, fourth value: possibly 129.705 rather than 129.715, which would make the written mean 129.807 exact. Otherwise Gauss's mean is off by 0.002.
The brace on 22 March groups the five bar-free readings, labelled 'ohne gr Stab', with mean 128.9446. The two values 126.457 and 130.585 are labelled 'gr St. NU' and 'NO' respectively.
The crossed-out marginal note near the top reads something like '50h/7 20' (struck through). It is likely an archival or foliation note, not part of the computation.
Headings 'März 20 Gr. Stab N. unten' and 'März 21 Gr. Stab, N. oben' are written with abbreviated 'unte'/'obe' endings in the hand.
